newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Zambia to aim for 5.5-pct real GDP growth in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Zambia to aim for 5.5-pct real GDP growth in 1997.

text.p: The Zambian government said on Friday it would seek 5.5-percent growth in 1997 real gross domestic product (GDP) after 6.4-percent growth in 1996.
"The main thrust of this year's economic policy is a 5.5-ercent growth in real GDP, while maintaining macro-economic stability," finance minister Ronald Penza said in his 1997 budget speech.
"To maintain macro-economic stablity and to achieve the inflation target, it will be important to maintain a tight fiscal and monetary stance," Penza said.
Penza said he expected inflation to drop to 15 percent by year end from 35 percent at 1996-end.
He said broad money growth must also be kept within the expected real GDP growth and the inflation target.
"Furthermore, government spending will be focused on those areas that support growth. In this regard, it will be necessary to run an overall budget surplus of about one percent of GDP," he said.
Government spending would focus on the road rehabilitation programme, which would be allocated 30 billion kwacha ($22.7 million), agriculture and the provision of social services.
Penza said the public sector reform programme, which was suspended last year for lack of finances, would be sped up this year to reduce the government's wage bill.
He said the government would encourage public servants to opt for retirement.

He said the 6.4-percent growth in 1996 came mostly from agriculture, which took 28.7 percent, followed by non-traditional exports with 23 percent, tourism with 17.7 percent, commerce and trade with 13 percent, mining with 12.2 percent and manufacturing with 2.5 percent.
